# BIOBUZZ rules: what the simulator enforces

<!-- Generated by `node tools/rules-doc.js` from src/field/biobuzz/rules.js.
     Edit the catalogue, not this file. -->

All forty Game Rules from the BIOBUZZ V1 manual, and what this simulator does about
each one. The point of listing the ones it cannot check is that the gaps are then
visible: a rule missing from a list is a surprise at an event, and a rule marked
"cannot be violated here" is a known limit.

Of the forty: **11 are officiated live**, 1 is detected and
reported without being scored, 1 is checked at setup,
8 cannot happen here, 3 are outside the physics,
and 16 are about people and events rather than ROBOTS.

## Penalties (Table 10-4)

A MINOR FOUL is a credit of **5 points** and a MAJOR FOUL a credit
of **20 points** "towards the opponent’s MATCH point total". That
wording matters and the score follows it: a foul you commit is added to the other
ALLIANCE’S total, it is not deducted from yours, so a foul can never take you below
the points you earned. In the panel it is the PENALTY row, and it reads as points
gained from the opponent’s fouls.

## STRATEGIC, without reading minds

A dozen rules read "VERBAL WARNING. MAJOR FOUL and YELLOW CARD, if STRATEGIC", and
STRATEGIC is a REFEREE’S judgement of intent. Section 10.6 says how that judgement
is reached, though: "multiple warnings are given during an individual MATCH for the
same violation that individually can be perceived to be accidental". So that is the
model -- the first instances draw a warning, and a repeat inside the same MATCH is
STRATEGIC and takes the foul. It is the manual’s own test, and it is the right
lesson anyway: doing it once is forgivable, doing it repeatedly is not.

## Officiated during a MATCH (11)

The REFEREE watches for these every step and assesses the manual’s own penalty. This is where the practice value is: a MAJOR FOUL is 20 points, which is ten elements in a CELL.

| Rule | | Violation | What the sim does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **G401** | Do not interact with a ROBOT during AUTO. | VERBAL WARNING; MAJOR FOUL and YELLOW CARD per MATCH if STRATEGIC | The sim deliberately leaves the sticks live during AUTO, because taking them away would make the period unusable until pasted AUTO code lands. So driving in AUTO is possible and is called: the first second of it is a warning, sustained driving is the foul. |
| **G402** | No AUTO opponent interference. | MAJOR FOUL per MATCH; MAJOR FOUL and YELLOW CARD if STRATEGIC | Called on the detectable half: during AUTO, contacting an opponent ROBOT while across the centre line on their side of the FIELD. Crossing alone is reported as advisory, because the manual only says it "may be seen as STRATEGIC". |
| **G403** | ROBOTS are motionless between AUTO and TELEOP. | VERBAL WARNING; MAJOR FOUL and YELLOW CARD per MATCH if STRATEGIC | Powered movement during the 8-second transition. Measured as commanded effort -- drive duty or a running MECHANISM -- not as motion, because the rule exempts movement "due to inertia, gravity, or de-energizing of actuators". |
| **G404** | ROBOTS are motionless at the end of TELEOP. | VERBAL WARNING; MAJOR FOUL and YELLOW CARD per MATCH if STRATEGIC | The same test as G403, after the buzzer. Worth practising: a flywheel left spinning is powered movement, and the habit of letting go of everything at 0:00 is the one the rule is asking for. |
| **G405** | Keep SCORING ELEMENTS in bounds. | MAJOR FOUL per SCORING ELEMENT | Every element that leaves the FIELD is attributed from what last touched it. A LAUNCHED element is a scoring attempt and a squeeze between two ROBOTS is a ROBOT-to-ROBOT interaction -- the rule exempts both by name -- so only an element a ROBOT carried, shoved or spat over the wall is a foul. Either way it comes back: see Section 10.8.2 and `BiobuzzField.returnElements`. |
| **G407** | No more than 4 at a time. | VERBAL WARNING; MAJOR FOUL and YELLOW CARD per MATCH if STRATEGIC | Counts the elements a ROBOT has taken ownership of -- its intake and anything its grabber holds. Deliberately not bulldozed or deflected elements, both of which the rule lists as not CONTROL. |
| **G408** | Do not CONTROL opponent NECTAR. | VERBAL WARNING; YELLOW CARD per MATCH if STRATEGIC | A NECTAR of the other colour held by a ROBOT. No foul points at any tier -- the manual gives this one a warning and then a card -- so it shows in the citation list without moving the score. Mostly unreachable by default, because the intake senses the colour and refuses one, which is what a real ROBOT does with an element that is worth nothing to it. Turn "Intake rejects opponent NECTAR" off to drill the hazard, and then steering around the other colour is the driver’s job. |
| **G409** | Do not catch SCORING ELEMENTS. | VERBAL WARNING; YELLOW CARD per MATCH if STRATEGIC | Elements let go by a TIPPING HIVE are flagged until they touch anything that is not the ROBOT -- the TILES, a wall, the frame, another element -- and a ROBOT contact while the flag is up is the catch. Two are forgiven, which matches the rule’s own examples: one or two POLLEN landing on a ROBOT driving past is not a violation, sitting under the HIVE waiting is. |
| **G410** | NECTAR only goes into FLOWERS with one minute left. | MAJOR FOUL per NECTAR | Counted on entry to the FLOWER scoring volume, not prevented -- the element still scores and the ALLIANCE takes the foul, which is how a REFEREE handles it. |
| **G417** | ROBOTS may not meddle with the HIVE Structure. | VERBAL WARNING; MAJOR FOUL and YELLOW CARD per MATCH if STRATEGIC | Two detectors, matching the rule’s own examples. Driving into the HIVE frame above a walking pace is example A/B ("ramming into the HIVE frame at high-speed"); a LAUNCHED element striking the *opponent’s* HIVE is example D ("impeding the TIP of an opponent’s HIVE by LAUNCHING at it"). Missing your own CELL and hitting its outside is example H and explicitly not a violation, so it is not called. |
| **G421** | There is a 3-count on PINS. | MAJOR FOUL per instance, and another every 3 seconds uncorrected | The full count, with all three end conditions and both pause clauses: the count pauses at 2 ft of separation and resumes if the pinner closes back in, pauses once either ROBOT has moved 2 ft from where the pin began, and ends outright if the pinner gets pinned. |

## Detected and reported, never scored (1)

The sim can see something that looks like this, but the manual’s test is whether a REFEREE judged the action STRATEGIC. Shown to the driver with no points attached -- putting a foul on a heuristic teaches people to avoid the heuristic.

| Rule | | Violation | What the sim does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **G411** | Do not hoard SCORING ELEMENTS. | MAJOR FOUL and YELLOW CARD per MATCH | Corralling is detectable -- a cluster of loose elements with an ALLIANCE ROBOT parked on it -- but the rule turns on STRATEGICALLY denying access, and the GARDENS start with a legitimate cluster in them. This one has no warning tier, so a false positive would be 20 points and a card off a heuristic. Reported, never scored. |

## Checked before the MATCH (1)

Staging, rather than play.

| Rule | | Violation | What the sim does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **G304** | ROBOTS must be set up correctly on the FIELD. | Corrected before the MATCH; MINOR FOUL if not | `Match.checkStartingPosition` tests all five clauses -- own side, inside the perimeter, touching the wall, clear of every FLOWER, out of the LOADING ZONE -- and `BiobuzzGame.stageRobots` only ever uses a position that passes it. |

## Cannot be violated here (8)

Each of these names the mechanism that makes it impossible, so the claim can be checked rather than taken on trust.

| Rule | | Violation | What the sim does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **G305** | Teams must select an OpMode. | VERBAL WARNING; MINOR FOUL if not corrected | An op-mode is always selected and initialised: the sim has nothing else to run. |
| **G412** | ROBOTS must be under control. | DISABLED and VERBAL WARNING | About hazards *outside* the FIELD: flailing over the wall, knocking over a DRIVER STATION, contacting FIELD STAFF. The sim has a closed perimeter and nothing outside it, and an element that leaves is G405. |
| **G415** | Watch your ARENA interaction. | VERBAL WARNING; YELLOW CARD if STRATEGIC | Grabbing, attaching to or suspending from an ARENA element. No mechanism here can take hold of anything but a SCORING ELEMENT, which the rule exempts, and the concave FLOWER-alignment shape it explicitly allows is what the grabber archetypes use. |
| **G416** | ROBOTS have construction limits. | MAJOR FOUL per instance | The R105 expansion volume during a MATCH. The sim’s chassis has a fixed footprint and its mechanisms do not extend past it, so the limit is never approached. |
| **G418** | ROBOTS may not meddle with FLOWERS. | VERBAL WARNING; MAJOR FOUL and YELLOW CARD per MATCH if STRATEGIC | Both clauses are built into the geometry. `Flower.interactBall` only captures an element descending through the top ring, so there is no other way in; `Flower.removeBottom` refuses anything wider than the 3.55 in retrieval gap, so a NECTAR cannot come out at all and a NECTAR at the bottom plugs the tube. |
| **G426** | Humans may not enter NECTAR onto the FIELD early. | MINOR FOUL per NECTAR | The release schedule is the gate: `BiobuzzField.unlockNectar` hands over one NECTAR per TIP and the remainder at 60 seconds, and `introduceNectar` returns null when nothing is unlocked. There is no way to enter one early. |
| **G427** | Humans, only enter NECTAR via the LOADING ZONE. | MINOR FOUL per NECTAR | `introduceNectar` is the only path onto the FIELD, and it places the NECTAR at rest on the TILES inside its own ALLIANCE’S LOADING ZONE -- contacting the TILE first, as clause C requires, by its own colour, with no tool. |
| **G428** | Humans, do not remove SCORING ELEMENTS from the FIELD. | MINOR FOUL per SCORING ELEMENT | No human hand can pick anything up. The only route off the FIELD is a ROBOT putting it there, which is G405, and FIELD STAFF putting it back, which is Section 10.8.2. |

## Not modelled (3)

A real ROBOT could violate these and this one cannot, because the physics has no model for what the rule is about. Damage and tipping over are the whole list.

| Rule | | Violation | What the sim does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **G406** | Do not damage or make a mess in the ARENA. | VERBAL WARNING; MAJOR FOUL and YELLOW CARD if STRATEGIC | Nothing here can be damaged: the TILES, the walls and the structures are rigid and permanent. Ramming the HIVE frame is caught, but as G417. |
| **G419** | Do not damage an opponent ROBOT. | VERBAL WARNING; MAJOR FOUL and YELLOW CARD per instance if STRATEGIC | No damage model. A ROBOT here is a rigid box with a drivetrain: there is nothing to disconnect, bend or switch off, so a high-speed ram is only a collision. |
| **G420** | Do not tip or entangle. | VERBAL WARNING; MAJOR FOUL and YELLOW CARD per instance if STRATEGIC | The chassis is a planar 3-DOF body -- x, y and heading -- so it cannot leave the floor or fall over, and nothing on it can entangle. The load-transfer model does report when a ROBOT would tip, but it does not then tip it. |

## DRIVE TEAM conduct (10)

There are no humans in the sim beyond the one hand that rolls NECTAR into the LOADING ZONE, so there is nothing to watch.

| Rule | | Violation | What the sim does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **G101** | Humans, stay off the FIELD during the MATCH. | VERBAL WARNING | There is no human body in the sim to put on the TILES. |
| **G102** | Be careful when interacting with ARENA elements. | VERBAL WARNING; YELLOW CARD if STRATEGIC | Climbing on, hanging from and manipulating the ARENA are human actions. |
| **G201** | Be a good person. | per Section 10.6 | Conduct toward people. Nothing to model. |
| **G202** | Follow the Competition Integrity Contract. | per Section 10.6 | A team-level undertaking, signed before the event. |
| **G204** | Do not expect to gain by doing others harm. | per Section 10.6 | Actions aimed at forcing an opponent to violate a rule. Turns entirely on intent, and the manual assigns the opponent’s penalty to the instigator -- a call no detector can make. |
| **G205** | Egregious or exceptional violations. | Head REFEREE discretion, up to RED CARD | The rule that exists so the Head REFEREE is not bound by the list. |
| **G422** | DRIVE TEAM stays in the ALLIANCE AREA. | VERBAL WARNING; MINOR FOUL per instance if STRATEGIC | Where the people stand. |
| **G423** | DRIVE COACHES and other teams: hands off the controls. | VERBAL WARNING; MINOR FOUL per instance if STRATEGIC | Who is holding the gamepad. The sim has one seat and cannot see who is in it. |
| **G424** | DRIVE COACHES, SCORING ELEMENTS are off limits. | VERBAL WARNING; MINOR FOUL per instance if STRATEGIC | A human touching an element. The only human action modelled is entering NECTAR. |
| **G425** | DRIVE TEAMS, watch your reach. | VERBAL WARNING; MINOR FOUL per instance if STRATEGIC | Reaching into the FIELD. `introduceNectar` places a NECTAR on the TILES in the LOADING ZONE and touches nothing else, which is the compliant version of the one reach the sim performs. |

## Event logistics (6)

Decided outside a single MATCH: queueing, inspection, the Head REFEREE.

| Rule | | Violation | What the sim does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **G203** | Show up to your MATCHES. | Surrogate / no-show handling | Attendance at a scheduled MATCH. The sim starts when you press start. |
| **G301** | Do not delay MATCHES. | VERBAL WARNING; MAJOR FOUL for the upcoming MATCH | Queueing and field reset, between MATCHES. |
| **G302** | Limit what you bring to the FIELD. | VERBAL WARNING; MINOR FOUL if not corrected | What fits in the ALLIANCE AREA. Nothing is carried to the FIELD here. |
| **G303** | ROBOTS on the FIELD must come ready to play. | VERBAL WARNING; not permitted to play | Inspection, battery, and the ROBOT being present and MATCH-ready. The sim’s ROBOT is always inspected and always has a battery -- which is modelled, and sags. |
| **G413** | ROBOTS must stop when instructed. | RED CARD | There is no REFEREE channel to instruct a stop, and no reason to ignore one. |
| **G414** | ROBOTS must be identifiable. | VERBAL WARNING; YELLOW CARD if STRATEGIC | Team numbers and ALLIANCE markings, which the renderer assigns and cannot lose. |

## Where this lives in the code

- `src/field/biobuzz/rules.js` -- the catalogue above, and the penalty values.
- `src/field/biobuzz/Referee.js` -- the detectors for the live rules.
- `src/field/biobuzz/Match.js` -- owns the REFEREE and folds the penalty into the score.
- `src/field/biobuzz/BiobuzzField.js` -- Section 10.8.2, returning elements that left.
- `test/biobuzz-rules.test.js` -- checks the list against the manual and every detector.
